rationale: Round 1 built, ran, and preserved correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round raises aggressiveness across all seven passes: the program is tiny (37 functions, ~3.8 KB text) and C++-heavy with many small methods (addPredators, process, addPrey, addObstacles all ~300 B), meaning a broad mix of passes yields maximal diversity with modest absolute size/runtime cost. BCF and FLA get the highest security/diversity weights as the core control-flow transformations, and their lowered RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights let them fire on the small hot functions where loops (ocean movement/update) tolerate flattening and bogus branching well. IBR and SUB are favored next for opcode/layout diversity at low risk; SPLIT is kept enabled primarily as a diversity amplifier that pre-conditions FLA/BCF by increasing basic-block count. ICALL keeps a moderately high RuntimeCost weight (0.5) so indirect dispatch concentrates on the few larger functions where call-graph indirection pays off most, avoiding per-call overhead in the hot simulation loop, and its CorrectnessRisk stays low-moderate given the clean prior run. IGV rounds out the set with data-level obfuscation; all CorrectnessRisk weights remain below 0.15 since the measured evidence shows the pipeline is stable on this sample, inviting the optimizer to apply all seven passes broadly while still gating extremes.
